r.$description: Radius: moderate, disciplined. Sharp enough to read bold, soft enough to be usable.

2xl.$description: splash tile: distinct from xl's app icon tile

scrim.$description:
Overlay scrim: backdrop for anything that covers the app (ArenaDialog,
ConfirmDialog, ArenaCommandPalette, ArenaOnboarding). The blur is what separates a
modal from a coachmark: ArenaDialog/ArenaConfirmDialog/ArenaCommandPalette pair the scrim
with --scrim-blur, ArenaOnboarding uses the scrim alone, because a tour that
blurs the product it is touring defeats itself.

loop.$description:
Cyclical motion. Deliberately not part of dur: a transition is a
response to an action and is measured in the hundred-millisecond range; a loop
reports that work is ongoing and is measured in seconds. Merging them would
repeat the fs/dz mistake the type scale already retired. `reduced` is the one
value prefers-reduced-motion slows every working loop to; it was copied into
three files before it was a token.

brand.$description: Rotor: slow enough to read as presence rather than progress

reduced.$description: What a working loop slows to under prefers-reduced-motion. Motion that reports work slows rather than stopping: a frozen spinner reads as a hung process.

brand-reduced.$description: Rotor's reduced step: the brand mark is three times slower again, because it is decoration that happens to also mean 'alive'

tint.$description:
How much of a colour a tinted surface keeps, as the percentage a color-mix()
keeps of it. A number carrying a % render hint rather than a dimension, because
DTCG admits only px and rem in a dimension, the same reason tracking is a number
carrying an em hint. Script-readable: both layers build the color-mix() as a
string in JS, so the ratio has to arrive as a number rather than as a custom
property. These are the tints of an IDENTITY, a colour that stands for a thing;
the per-hue -soft aliases in colors.css are a different family and stay there,
because each is tuned to its own hue rather than shared across all eight.

area.$description: Fill under a line chart's series. A tint, never a gradient.

soft.$description:
The surface an identity colour stands on: light enough that text at the
body contrast keeps its ratio over it, which is why it is well under area.

edge.$description:
The hairline around that surface. It reads as the same colour only because
it is roughly twice soft: a border at the surface's own ratio disappears.
